$comment: Designed so task success is heavily dependent on CP integration:
On both, CPs replace primary generation — losing a CP creates
a deficit that intra-sector gossip + local-gen fallback alone cannot recover.
* Failures: high failure_lambda + small max_failures + tight
slack_budget_pct so the system actually has something to recover from.
Generator-class failures bias toward CP loss (CPs are the dominant
* Ablations: enable_cross_sector_coalitions toggled on/off with the
rest of the stack identical so the comparison isolates L2.5 effect.
* Short sim window (6 s) + tight task_timeout (240 s) keeps the local
runner under 10 minutes wallclock on a workstation.
Cells: 4 experiments x cells -> 24 tasks at ~12 s sim each.
name: cp_coalition_eval

experiments.$comment: Headline ablation: same scenario, flag flipped.  Tight slack + multi-failure forces the cross-sector layer to actually do work.
experiments.name: xs_coalition_ablation

experiments.$comment: Mixed failures (branch + generator) on the same headline grid so the cross-sector path is exercised alongside line-loading + intra-sector deficits.
experiments.name: xs_coalition_mixed_failures

experiments.$comment: Stack isolation: per-sector L2 coalitions off so the cross-sector layer is the only coalition mechanism.  If L2.5 is doing real work this configuration should beat the doubly-disabled baseline on cp_dependent grids.
experiments.name: xs_only_vs_no_coalitions

experiments.$comment: Negative control: same flag-on/off ablation on a grid where CPs do NOT replace primary generation.  Cross-sector coalitions should have a small effect because intra-sector gossip+local-gen fallback can recover most deficits on its own.
experiments.name: non_dependent_control
